resale_co.name: Continuing Certificate of Occupancy (CCO)
resale_co.lead_time: Inspection fee is paid in advance. The application is void after 45 days.
requirements: Smoke detectors in each bedroom, within 10 feet of bedroom areas and at least one per level including the basement and walk-up attic; battery units must be 10-year sealed
CO detectors within 10 feet of bedroom areas and kitchens, at least one per level including basements and walk-up attics
Fire extinguisher rated 2A:10BC, no more than 10 pounds, visibly mounted in the kitchen or within 10 feet of it toward an exit
911 post (4 x 4 inch, 6 feet, 2 feet in the ground) at the driveway entrance with 4-inch reflective numbers on each side
Tree limbs cut back at least 10 feet from the roof line
Handrails on stairways and stoops with 3 or more steps; guardrails on porches, decks and raised floors 30 inches or higher, spindles no more than 4 inches apart
No broken windows or doors, no holes in walls, no exterior damage or leaking roof
Switch plates and outlet covers in place, GFI outlets within 3 feet of kitchen and bathroom sinks, no bare wires, secure covered breaker panel
Working range with anti-tip device and other appliances working
Hot and cold running water without leaks, flushing toilets and working heat
Bathroom window or exhaust fan vented outside; water heater relief valve extension within 6 inches of the floor
Electric service wire and meter sound; no double-cylinder deadbolts on exterior doors
All code violations abated and all open construction, electrical, plumbing or fire permits closed
No rubbish or debris inside or out; all utilities on at the inspection
No more than 2 occupants per bedroom

fees.label: Continuing Certificate of Occupancy inspection (paid in advance)
Re-inspection (payable before or at the re-inspection)
fees.quote: RE-INSPECTION FEE $15.00. PAYABLE BEFORE OR AT RE-INSPECTION

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill in the Township of Pittsgrove Application and Continuing Certificate of Occupancy (mark "Resale", give the settlement date and the number of smoke detectors, CO detectors and extinguishers) and return it with the $40.00 inspection fee to the Housing/Zoning/Code Enforcement Office, 989 Centerton Road, Pittsgrove. The form records payment by check.

resale_co.notes: The live Township website (pittsgrovetownship.com) shows a SiteGround captcha to automated requests, so the Township pages and forms were read from Internet Archive copies: the Housing/Zoning/Code Enforcement page captured 2024-05-21 (original https://www.pittsgrovetownship.com/departments/housing-zoning-code-enforcement/) and the Continuing Certificate of Occupancy application captured 2024-06-30 (original https://www.pittsgrovetownship.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Application-and-Requirements-for-Continuing-Certificate-of-Occupancy-PDF.pdf). The application form (REV 2/13) has a "Resale" box and a settlement date line; its requirements page is dated Rev 9-22 and gives the $40.00 inspection fee and $15.00 re-inspection fee. The form says the application is void after 45 days and the certificate is non-transferable. The requirements page lists the office phone as (856) 358-2300 Ext. 24 and housing-zoning@pittsgrovetownship.com; the 2024 department page and Township directory give Edward Ramsay at ext 6029 and eramsay@pittsgrovetownship.com. Whether Edward Ramsay is still the official in 2026 was not confirmed. Rentals also need a Rental Registration Certificate ($15.00) and a certified water test report from the last five years (rental only); the Township has a rent control board.

requirements: Township CCO smoke sheet (effective January 1, 2019): battery smoke detectors must be 10-year sealed battery units
Smoke detectors in each bedroom as well as on each level (Township CCO list)
CO detectors within 10 feet of bedroom areas and kitchens, one per level (Township CCO list)
Township CCO list still asks for a 2A:10BC fire extinguisher, no more than 10 pounds, mounted in or within 10 feet of the kitchen

authorities.name: Pittsgrove Township Bureau of Fire Safety (smoke detector compliance through the Pittsgrove Township Zoning Office)
authorities.how_to_apply: No separate smoke/CO certificate application or fee was found. The Township Continuing Certificate of Occupancy application records smoke detectors, CO detectors and the fire extinguisher, and the state directory names the Pittsgrove Township Zoning Office for smoke detector compliance. Ask the Housing/Zoning/Code Enforcement Office whether the CCO inspection also serves as the smoke/CO certificate.

fire_cert.notes: Pittsgrove enforces the fire code locally (LEA registry code M). The state fire directory (listed there as Pittsgrove Township 1710, three fire companies) names Fire Official Charles Hughes at 989 Centerton Rd and "Pittsgrove Twp Zoning Office" for smoke detector compliance; it prints a direct phone (856) 207-2434 and a non-Township email for him. The Township directory (Internet Archive, July 2024) lists Charles Hughes for the Bureau of Fire Safety and as Construction Code Official at extension 6013 with chughes@pittsgrovetownship.com (from the mailto link); the Township main number is 856-358-2300 (page footer), and the extension 6013 is not joined to it here because the page prints them separately. No separate smoke/CO certificate fee was found; the smoke, CO and extinguisher checks appear to be part of the Continuing Certificate of Occupancy inspection. The Township still lists the fire extinguisher on its CCO requirements (Rev 9-22) and its smoke sheet prints the pre-2025 N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19 text; the state removed the extinguisher from the state requirement by P.L.2025, c.19. Pittsgrove also has a fire district (Board of Fire Commissioners) for fire service, but the registry lists the Township, not a district, as the fire code enforcing agency.

other_items.label: Open permits closed
other_items.detail: All open construction, electrical, plumbing or fire permits must be closed out and all code violations abated.

other_items.label: Utilities on
other_items.detail: All utilities must be on at the time of inspection.

Does the CCO inspection also issue the smoke/CO certificate, or is there a separate Bureau of Fire Safety certificate and fee?
